caveats: The figures describe NWSDB operations, not every water provider or household. Historical volume labels are rounded to million cubic metres; recomputing non-revenue water from them will not reproduce the unrounded underlying ratio. Non-revenue water includes more than physical leaks. Bacteriological pass rates describe tested samples, not population coverage or a guarantee for each connection. Table 5 wrongly labels staff per 1,000 connections as a percentage; figure 36 confirms that the measure is a staffing ratio. The original unit error is recorded in the affected cell notes. Overlapping table and figure observations must not be summed.
Figure observations retain rounded printed labels; table observations retain their additional decimal precision. Distinct report sections identify overlapping observations.
grain: One reported national utility measure, report section and year
notes: The NWSDB 2024 annual report prints ten-year series for water production and consumption, non-revenue water, staff per 1,000 connections and the share of water samples passing bacteriological tests. These labelled figure values are preserved along with the more precise 2023–2024 non-revenue-water and staffing figures in table 5.
